To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new class of orally active antitumour agents has been identified.

the in vitro antiproliferative activity of a set of 99 structurally diversified Garcinia xanthone analogues, based on gambogin, was evaluated and the most active compounds were selected for in vivo efficacy studies, which led to the identification of compound 112 as an orally active antitumour agent.

the design, synthesis, and in vitro antitumoral evaluation of a library of 99 Garcinia natural-productlike xanthones based upon gambogic acid led to the identification of a new class of orally active antitumoral agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new strategy for the design, synthesis, and evaluation of orally active antitumour agents.

the development of a novel strategy for the synthesis of xanthones based upon propargylation of a hydroxyxanthones, which can be applied to the synthesis of a large number of natural-product-like xanthonoids.
the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a new series of Garcinia xanthone derivatives as orally active antineoplastic agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the newly designed and synthesized xanthones have shown potent in vivo activity and are orally active, thus demonstrating the potential of this class of compounds as antitumor agents.
the strategy developed in this work is a useful tool for the design and synthesis of novel xanthone derivatives with potential antitumor activity.
a new series of natural-product-like Garcinia xanthones was designed and synthesized and a subset of 40 compounds was characterized for physicochemical properties and in vitro antitumour activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new strategy to design xanthones as potent orally active anticancer agents was developed.
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of the 99 xanthone analogues led to a new orally bioavailable antitumor lead compound.
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of the 99 xanthone derivatives led to the identification of a new class of orally active anticancer agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to design and synthesize orally active antitumors based on the xanthone scaffold.
the regioselectively propargylated xanthones can be used as a scaffold to design orally active xanthones.
it is possible to design and synthesize a large set of xanthone-based antitumor agents that are amenable to oral dosing.
